exemplars.:question/problem:
Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\mathbf{a}=\langle 1,2,0\rangle$, $\mathbf{b}=\langle 0,1,2\rangle$, and $\mathbf{c}=\langle -3,0,1\rangle$.

![A parallelepiped with three edge vectors a, b, and c](images/25/2597b48a010607fca71c551dbce8e9e2bbeda47d0892a582347ae1cdf19f1bf6.png)

The diagram is schematic and is not to scale.
exemplars.:question/worked-solution:
The volume is the absolute value of the scalar triple product:

$$
V=|\mathbf{a}\cdot(\mathbf{b}\times\mathbf{c})|.
$$

Use the edge vectors as the rows of a determinant. Expanding along the first row gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{a}\cdot(\mathbf{b}\times\mathbf{c})
&=\begin{vmatrix}1&2&0\\0&1&2\\-3&0&1\end{vmatrix}\\
&=1\begin{vmatrix}1&2\\0&1\end{vmatrix}-2\begin{vmatrix}0&2\\-3&1\end{vmatrix}+0\\
&=1(1\cdot1-2\cdot0)-2(0\cdot1-2(-3))\\
&=1-12=-11.
\end{aligned}
$$

The triple product is signed, but volume is nonnegative. Therefore

$$
V=|-11|=11.
$$

exemplars.:question/problem:
Suppose $\mathbf{a}\cdot(\mathbf{b}\times\mathbf{c})=-5$. Calculate the volume $V$ of the parallelepiped whose three edge vectors are $2\mathbf{b}$, $\mathbf{c}$, and $3\mathbf{a}$.

$V=${{volume}}
exemplars.:question/worked-solution:
The volume is the absolute value of the scalar triple product of the actual edge vectors:

$$
V=|(2\mathbf{b})\cdot(\mathbf{c}\times3\mathbf{a})|.
$$

Factor out the two scale factors. A cyclic change from $\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathbf{c}$ to $\mathbf{b},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{a}$ preserves the scalar triple product:

$$
\begin{aligned}
(2\mathbf{b})\cdot(\mathbf{c}\times3\mathbf{a})
&=6\,\mathbf{b}\cdot(\mathbf{c}\times\mathbf{a})\\
&=6\,\mathbf{a}\cdot(\mathbf{b}\times\mathbf{c})\\
&=6(-5)=-30.
\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, take the absolute value:

$$
V=|-30|=30.
$$

Scaling two different edges multiplies their scale factors; it does not add or square them.

First form the actual edge vectors component by component:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{u}=\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}&=\langle 1+(-1),2+1,1+2\rangle=\langle0,3,3\rangle,\\
\mathbf{v}=\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{b}&=\langle 1-(-1),2-1,1-2\rangle=\langle2,1,-1\rangle,\\
\mathbf{w}=\mathbf{c}&=\langle2,-1,1\rangle.
\end{aligned}
$$

The volume is $V=|\mathbf{u}\cdot(\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{w})|$. Use these edge vectors, rather than $\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathbf{c}$, as the determinant rows:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{u}\cdot(\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{w})
&=\begin{vmatrix}0&3&3\\2&1&-1\\2&-1&1\end{vmatrix}\\
&=0-3\begin{vmatrix}2&-1\\2&1\end{vmatrix}+3\begin{vmatrix}2&1\\2&-1\end{vmatrix}\\
&=-3(2\cdot1-(-1)\cdot2)+3(2(-1)-1\cdot2)\\
&=-3(4)+3(-4)\\
&=-24.
\end{aligned}
$$

Taking the absolute value gives

$$
V=|-24|=24.
$$

The two mixed edges are not parallel simply because both are made from $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$. Subtracting the vectors also requires subtracting each signed component.
